stories.title: Jets and Titans Fans Trade Barbs Before Week 1 Clash
stories.one_line: Fans from the New York Jets and Tennessee Titans are firing up the hype for their September 13 matchup at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, with kickoff at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Titans supporters boast about new head coach Robert Saleh—formerly of the Jets—and added ex-Jets defenders, even floating a wild bet to walk from MetLife to Nissan Stadium if they lose. Jets fans counter by pointing to both teams' rough records, like the Titans' 19-49 over four seasons, while memes of Forrest Gump and past game clips keep the fun going as everyone admits neither side has much bragging room yet.

stories.title: Tennessee Taps True Freshman Faizon Brandon as Starting QB
stories.one_line: The Volunteers named five-star recruit Faizon Brandon their starting quarterback for the 2026 season, marking the first true freshman season opener since 2004. The 6-foot-4 dual-threat from North Carolina beat out redshirt freshman George MacIntyre, thanks to his standout high school record of 35-1 with two state titles and relentless work ethic praised by coach Josh Heupel. Brandon debuts against Furman on Sept. 5, facing a tough SEC slate including Texas and Auburn, with fans buzzing about his potential in a talented offense.

stories.title: Philly Debated as Worst Major City for College Football Passion
stories.one_line: Crossing Broad's Kevin Kinkead pointed to Temple's middling status in a rented NFL stadium, split Penn State support due to distance and past issues, and the Eagles and Phillies dominating attention as reasons Philly lags. Many agreed the Northeast overall lacks college football buzz, with one fan calling it 'sad,' while others noted Penn State's top atmosphere in Pennsylvania or compared it to quieter scenes in Boston and New York. Temple's rare 10-win seasons in 2015 and 2016 stand out as exceptions in a history of struggles, amid pro sports' heavy pull on local loyalty.

stories.one_line: The Locked On Big 12 podcast projected Texas Tech to top the standings, with BYU undefeated in conference play, West Virginia shocking everyone, and Oklahoma State proving doubters wrong. CFB Home's Week 0 power rankings put BYU first, TCU second, and Texas Tech eighth, prompting fans to call them egregious or randomly generated. While betting markets favor Texas Tech to repeat as champions ahead of BYU and Utah, the lists highlight the parity and upset potential in the 16-team league after last year's turnover.
